doc.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Anita O'Day and other singers at Blues Alley
summary: Stories about Anita O'Day's short weeks and working with Teddy King and Maxine Sullivan while barely able to read.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Oh yeah, well, she’s nothing if she’s not interesting. And she had a good week though. She had some trouble there, she had a drummer once who quit on Tuesday night, he said — I think his name is John Poole. And he said, “I just can’t stand any more of these two day weeks.” She’d go in and get fired by Tuesday. But she had settled down.
She was a little strung out sometimes, wasn’t she?
Yeah. She was. A great singer, oh please. And Teddy King sang there, Maxine Sullivan, and I worked with all these people. And I was like a sponge at this point. I mean they © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
were bringing in music and at this point I was just barely learning how to read and I was trying to figure out what a C seventh was and—
Is that right and you’re playing behind these people?
